chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Salt said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the young girl whose father marries her off: does she have authority (to accept or reject) when she reaches maturity? He said: No. And I asked him about the virgin who reaches the maturity of women: does she have authority with her father? He said: She has no authority with her father as long as she is not married off (thayyibat).
ai.seo_question: Does a father have the right to marry off his minor daughter without her consent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (AS) distinguishes between a minor girl whose father's marriage contract remains binding upon her maturity, and a virgin who has reached maturity but remains unmarried (thayyibat), who retains the right to choose. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that while paternal authority persists for those married off in minority, a mature virgin retains her independent agency unless she explicitly consents otherwise, reflecting the principle of 'ghinm' (independence) in marital contracts.
